evidenceRegister.text:
[Page 1]
Northwind Resources Group - FY2025 Climate and Sustainability Extract Governance: The Board Risk and Sustainability Committee reviews climate-related risks and opportunities quarterly, as set out in its charter updated in 2025. The Chief Risk Officer reports directly to this Committee at each meeting. Two non-executive directors hold relevant environmental qualifications. Executive remuneration does not currently include a climate-linked component. Strategy: The Group has identified physical risks including flooding at its Queensland coastal facilities and transition risks from carbon pricing reforms in key export markets. Risks are assessed over short (to 2027), medium (to 2035) and long-term (to 2050) horizons. A transition plan has not yet been finalised. Risk Management: Climate risks are recorded in the Group Risk Register and assessed using the same likelihood and consequence matrix applied to all material risks, integrating climate into the enterprise risk framework. Metrics and Targets: Scope 1 emissions for FY2025 were 412,000 tCO2-e and Scope 2 emissions were 58,000 tCO2-e, calculated using the GHG Protocol on an operational control basis. Scope 3 emissions have not yet been measured. The Group has not yet set a formal emissions reduction target with a base year. Social: The Group reports a workplace safety Total Recordable Injury Frequency Rate of 4.2 per million hours worked for FY2025, down from 5.1 in FY2024. Workforce diversity data and supply chain human rights processes are not disclosed.

Northwind Resources Group - FY2025 Climate and Sustainability Extract Governance: The Board Risk and Sustainability Committee reviews climate-related risks and opportunities quarterly, as set out in its charter updated in 2025. The Chief Risk Officer reports directly to this Committee at each meeting. Two non-executive directors hold relevant environmental qualifications. Executive remuneration does not currently include a climate-linked component. Strategy: The Group has identified physical risks including flooding at its Queensland coastal facilities and transition risks from carbon pricing reforms in key export markets. Risks are assessed over short (to 2027), medium (to 2035) and long-term (to 2050) horizons. A transition plan has not yet been finalised. Risk Management: Climate risks are recorded in the Group Risk Register and assessed using the same likelihood and consequence matrix applied to all material risks, integrating climate into the enterprise risk framework. Metrics and Targets: Scope 1 emissions for FY2025 were 412,000 tCO2-e and Scope 2 emissions were 58,000 tCO2-e, calculated using the GHG Protocol on an operational control basis. Scope 3 emissions have not yet been measured. The Group has not yet set a formal emissions reduction target with a base year. Social: The Group reports a workplace safety Total Recordable Injury Frequency Rate of 4.2 per million hours worked for FY2025, down from 5.1 in FY2024. Workforce diversity data and supply chain human rights processes are not disclosed.
